findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket are stored unencrypted by default, exposing potentially sensitive report data at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing bucket ACL / public access controls
findings.description: No acl attribute or public access block is set, so the bucket may default to being accessible in ways not intended, and there is no explicit private ACL enforcing restricted access.
The bucket stores ledger export data (likely financial) without any server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding model artifacts, so data is stored unencrypted.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operational runbook data (which may contain sensitive operational details) is stored unencrypted.

The uploaded object does not specify server-side encryption (kms_key_id or server_side_encryption) and is placed into a bucket that itself lacks default encryption, resulting in the vendor roster file being stored in cleartext.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be deleted without protection, which combined with lack of versioning increases risk of irrecoverable data loss/tampering for archival data.
